text: 我们其实无法反驳一件零售违法批发却合法的事情。
en: We actually cannot refute the fact that retail is illegal yet wholesale is legal.

text: 先说明一下，该回答是淡老师发表了长篇大论邀请我答题，属于被迫营业。
en: First, let me clarify: this answer came about because Teacher Dan posted a long-winded piece inviting me to answer, so it counts as being pressed into service against my will.

text: 新加坡是卖淫合法化的国家，红灯区就在芽笼，这个著名红灯区，其实是一条只有长约1公里的大道，芽笼巷子分为单巷和双巷，单巷一般是美食，双巷就是大家眼里神秘的红灯区。
en: Singapore is a country where prostitution is legalised, and the red-light district lies in Geylang. This famous red-light district is in fact just a thoroughfare roughly one kilometre long. Geylang's lanes are split into single lanes and double lanes — the single lanes are mostly food, whilst the double lanes are the mysterious red-light district in everyone's eyes.

text: 单巷里是数不清的小吃店、会馆、寺庙等与情色无关的产业，而双巷则是酒廊、情色场所这些充满诱惑的幻想乡。
en: The single lanes house countless snack stalls, clan associations, temples and other industries unrelated to vice, whilst the double lanes are lounges and sex venues — a land of fantasy brimming with temptation.

text: 新加坡卖淫合法化，但从事卖淫的不能是本地人，卖淫女作为一种特殊职业，从是东南亚其他国家，比如菲律宾，泰国，印尼等引进的一种持有特殊工作准证。
en: Prostitution is legalised in Singapore, but those who practise it cannot be locals. Prostitutes, as a special occupation, are brought in from other Southeast Asian countries — such as the Philippines, Thailand and Indonesia — on a special work permit.

text: 这些情色行业工作者只能在新加坡待两年，时间一到就必须遣返回去。
en: These sex-industry workers may stay in Singapore for only two years, and the moment that period ends they must be repatriated.

text: 而且为了限制情色行业的发展，这些性工作者不允许和本地人结婚，再次来新加坡也不能从事以前的工作。
en: Moreover, to curb the growth of the sex industry, these sex workers are not permitted to marry locals, and should they return to Singapore they may not take up their former work.

text: 在芽笼，经政府认证的合法工作者有1300名左右，她们有着严格的行业规定，必须接受两周一次的体检。
en: In Geylang, there are roughly 1,300 government-certified legal workers, who are bound by strict industry rules and must submit to a medical check-up once every two weeks.

text: 当然新加坡除了芽笼还有一种地方叫“花场”。
en: Of course, besides Geylang, Singapore also has a kind of place called 'flower venues'.

text: 花场里面除了女性还有男性，也就是新加坡版的“白马会所”。
en: Flower venues contain not only women but also men — they are, in other words, Singapore's version of the 'White Horse Club'.

text: 在男花场工作的男性，主要是来自中国，也有少数外国人。
en: The men who work in male flower venues mainly come from China, with a small minority of foreigners.

text: 这种叫歌星，也是拿“黄卡”的一种特殊工作准证。
en: These are called 'singers', and they too hold a 'yellow card', a special type of work permit.

text: 在新加坡花场消费的女性群体大概有这么几类：本地Anuty、富二代留学生、在新加坡的单身妈妈和外国游客。
en: The women who patronise Singapore's flower venues fall roughly into a few groups: local Aunties, wealthy second-generation international students, single mothers in Singapore, and foreign tourists.

text: 而她们去男花场的目的无非就是排遣寂寞、寻求刺激。
en: And their reasons for visiting male flower venues are nothing more than dispelling loneliness and seeking excitement.

text: 在新加坡的男花场，想要赚得多就要讨好老板、讨好顾客、猛喝酒，被客人带走做不可描述的事情。
en: In Singapore's male flower venues, to earn more one must curry favour with the boss, curry favour with the clients, drink heavily, and be taken away by customers to do unspeakable things.

text: 这些男性工作满两年之后就会被驱除出境，不得因为同样的工作原因再次入境新加坡。
en: Once these men have completed two years of work they are deported and may not re-enter Singapore for the same line of work.

text: 看到这里，不知道大家看明白了没？
en: Having read this far, I wonder whether everyone has understood.

text: 卖淫合法化的新加坡，不会让本地人来做这样的工作，是从东南亚一些其他国家引进“黄卡”。
en: In legalised-prostitution Singapore, locals are not allowed to do this work; the 'yellow cards' are imported from various other Southeast Asian countries.

text: 而这些人，在“人人平等”的新加坡政府眼中，和孟加拉外劳无异，从来没有作为平等主体被对待过。
en: And these people, in the eyes of Singapore's 'all are equal' government, are no different from Bangladeshi foreign labourers, and have never been treated as equal agents.

text: 说句难听的，就是需要你的时候就让你入境，用过之后就像破抹布一样被丢弃了…
en: To put it harshly, they let you in when they need you, and once you have been used you are discarded like a tattered rag…

text: 卖淫不是不能合法，但是色情从业者，永远没有办法实现与普通公民一样的对等权利。
en: Prostitution may well be legalised, but those in the sex trade can never achieve the equal rights of ordinary citizens.

text: 现在遮遮掩掩的，从东莞“打工”回家还能找个老实人嫁了，如果这一切都公开化和合法化之后呢？
en: At present, under cover, they can return home from 'working' in Dongguan and still find an honest man to marry — but what if all of this were made public and legalised?

text: 这些人不可能永远吃青春饭，被行业淘汰过后又该何去何从？
en: These people cannot trade on their youth forever; once weeded out by the industry, where are they to go?

text: 试问，谁能这么头铁，接受这些色情从业者作为自己的朋友，亲人，甚至伴侣呢？
en: Let me ask: who would be so hard-headed as to accept these sex workers as their friend, relative, or even partner?

text: 差不多是十年以前，那时候的我是支持性交易合法化的。
en: Almost ten years ago, the me of that time supported the legalisation of sex work.

text: 先别急着骂，这个问题说来话长。
en: Don't rush to condemn me — this is a long story.

text: 我们从一个日经问题说起，知乎微博虎扑上你们可能都见过：就是让你吃一口屎，给你一万元，你干不干的。
en: Let us begin with a question asked daily that you have likely seen on Zhihu, Weibo and Hupu: if you were offered ten thousand yuan to eat a mouthful of shit, would you do it?

text: 平心而论，大多数人高估我国人均收入水平了，这个问题几乎没啥争议性，有项服务叫毒龙，二线红灯区只要200元，还包全套，放在你的人生和阶层去做这种事情是难以想象的，但有大把大把的人正在干，偷偷摸摸冒着法律风险也要干。
en: To be fair, most people overestimate our per-capita income. This question is hardly controversial. There is a service called 'rimming': in second-tier red-light districts it costs just 200 yuan and includes the full package. To engage in such an act given your life and your class is unimaginable, yet huge numbers of people are doing it, furtively and at the risk of breaking the law.

text: 吃屎算什么，别说一万元，只要你长期持续供给，一千元也有人干。
en: What is eating shit compared with that? Never mind ten thousand yuan — as long as you keep supplying it steadily, there are people who would do it for a thousand.

text: 世界上有许多肮脏的交易，在未来很长一段时间内是无法彻底根除的。
en: There are many sordid transactions in this world that cannot be utterly rooted out for a long time to come.

text: 只要社会贫富差距仍在，而市场有这种需求，交易就会继续。
en: So long as the gap between rich and poor persists and the market demands it, the trade will go on.

text: 这并非是一个简单的道德问题，而是民生问题；不是价值命题，而是事实命题。
en: This is not a simple moral issue but a matter of people's livelihoods; not a value proposition but a factual one.

text: 我们冲他们吐口水也罢，骂完了再踩两脚也罢，在繁荣的背后滋生着许多病疮，这些病疮你不给它们治，他们也得自己去死熬着，现在普遍的做法是回避事实，否认需要，用秩序以及道德等叙事来抵消它，但收效有多大，我是保持怀疑态度的。
en: Whether we spit on them or curse them and then stamp on them twice more, behind the prosperity many ulcers fester; if you do not treat these ulcers, they simply have to suffer them until they die. The prevailing approach now is to evade the facts, deny the need, and use narratives of order and morality to offset it — but how much good that does, I remain sceptical about.

text: 在这一套话术里，性交易合法化不是为了让男人合法去爽，而是为了尽可能保护社会底层女性的安全，保证她们在白道不被罚款，在黑道不被殴打，能够安全而卑微地张开双腿，换口面包吃，世界上能当福利姬、拍两张照片就有舔狗打赏，加个微信就要花几百块钱的毕竟是少数。
en: Within this line of rhetoric, the legalisation of sex work is not so that men can legally get their kicks, but to protect bottom-rung women's safety as far as possible — ensuring they are not fined by the law and not beaten by the gangs, so they can safely and humbly spread their legs to earn a mouthful of bread. In this world, those who can be 'camgirls' — who take a couple of photos and get simps tipping them, charging hundreds just to be added on WeChat — are, after all, a minority.

text: 大家都是人，都要脸，不是走投无路，谁愿意这么作践自己。
en: We are all human and all have our dignity; if not driven into a dead end, who would willingly demean themselves like this?

text: 然后是第二个问题，在中国当小三犯不犯法？
en: Then the second question: in China, is being a 'third party' (mistress) against the law?

text: 答案是不犯法。
en: The answer is no.

text: 只要你们不非法同居。
en: So long as you do not live together unlawfully.

text: 早些年有个女权主义者，叫叶海燕。
en: Some years back there was a feminist called Haiyan Ye.

text: 喊出一句口号，叫“小三是有钱人的妓女，妓女是老百姓的小三。
en: She raised a slogan: "The mistress is the rich man's whore, and the whore is the common people's mistress."

text: ”同样是买卖性交易，你们不敢得罪权贵阶层，但是对广大工农阶级，你们疯狂打压，说这是卖淫，是嫖娼，要扫黄打非。
en: "It is equally the buying and selling of sex. You dare not offend the elite class, yet against the vast working and peasant classes you crack down furiously, calling it prostitution and whoring, saying we must sweep away pornography and vice."

text: 那些到城里打工的老百姓，老人孩子都在家等着吃饭，他们不一样，搞不起婚外情，养不起小三儿，只是去发廊、到浴室打个炮而已，200块钱的卑微买卖，对社会没有任何坏的影响，你们要给人家抓起来。
en: Those common folk who go to the city to labour, with aged parents and children waiting at home for food — they are different. They cannot manage an affair, cannot keep a mistress; they just go to a hair salon or a bathhouse for a quick screw, a humble 200-yuan deal that harms society in no way, yet you want to have them arrested.

text: 面对那些睡在安稳大床，睡在老爷们赠与的二套房三套房里的小三，从不明面要钱，而是收着香奈儿、普拉达的小三，你们制裁不了。
en: Confronted with those mistresses who sleep in comfortable large beds, in the second or third flats gifted by their sugar daddies, who never ask for money openly but accept Chanel and Prada — those mistresses you cannot punish.

text: 笑贫不笑娼，就是这么个现状。
en: They mock the poor, not the prostitutes — that is the reality we have.

text: 所以那时的我接受了这些话术，支持性交易合法化，因为我认为法制不是阶级压迫的工具，而应该对这个国家的公民一视同仁。
en: So the me of that time accepted this rhetoric and supported the legalisation of sex work, because I believed the legal system is not a tool of class oppression, but should treat this country's citizens without distinction.

text: 第三个问题，性交易算不算一种工作？
en: The third question: does sex work count as a kind of labour?

text: 出卖肉体这种批判看似有力，但说穿了，哪个工作不是在出卖肉体。
en: The critique of 'selling the body' seems forceful, but once you lay it bare, which job does not involve selling the body?

text: 做设计要出卖脑力，做施工要出卖体力，搬砖要出卖肩膀，坐办公室要出卖腰椎，陪酒的要出卖肠胃，熬夜的要出卖肝脏，你偏偏认为出卖生殖器是肮脏的，出卖其他身体器官是正义，好像谁没有在被这个社会压迫，谁没有在被资本压榨一样。
en: Doing design sells your brainpower, doing construction sells your physical strength, moving bricks sells your shoulders, sitting in an office sells your lumbar spine, accompanying drinkers sells your stomach, burning the midnight oil sells your liver — yet you insist that selling one's genitals is dirty whilst selling other body organs is righteous, as if no one were being oppressed by this society or squeezed by capital.

text: 当你们指责别人双腿一张、不劳而获的时候，我实在告诉你们，这不是道德问题，是阶层问题，那些大街上扫地的，下水道通渠的，垃圾场收废品的，许多人在心里未必就瞧得起他们，某些家长在教育孩子的时候，一样拿有色眼镜去把别人当反面例子，“你不好好学习将来就去送外卖”等等。
en: When you accuse others of spreading their legs and getting something for nothing, let me tell you plainly: this is not a moral issue but a class issue. Those who sweep the streets, clear the sewers, collect scrap at the dump — many people do not necessarily look up to them in their hearts. Some parents, when teaching their children, likewise view others through coloured spectacles as negative examples: 'if you don't study hard you'll end up delivering takeaway', and so on.

text: 好像出卖身体就是道德败坏，出卖脑力就是高贵人种一般。
en: It is as if selling the body is moral corruption, whilst selling one's brainpower marks one as a superior sort.

text: 承认吧，出卖什么和道德没有关系，是你的阶层蒙蔽了你的良心。
en: Admit it: what one sells has nothing to do with morality — it is your class that has blinded your conscience.

text: 我说这么多，是因为首页上大多数讨论与分析根本没有正面我们的阶层，而是基于某种道德，某种立场，某种性别，甚至是某种利益群体在发言。
en: I say all this because most of the discussion and analysis on the home page never confronts our class directly, but speaks from a certain morality, a certain stance, a certain gender, even a certain interest group.

text: 当初的我愤怒，我支持性交易合法化，仅仅是基于人本主义关怀。
en: The me of back then was angry; I supported the legalisation of sex work purely out of humanist concern.

text: 甚至到今天，我反对性交易合法化，同样也是基于人本主义关怀。
en: Even today, my opposition to the legalisation of sex work is likewise grounded in humanist concern.

text: 为什么反对？
en: Why oppose it?

text: 因为在平息一切情绪，悬置一切预设前提之后，我发现有一个问题，我说服不了我自己了。
en: Because, after quieting all emotion and suspending all presuppositions, I found a problem I could no longer talk myself past.

text: 性交易，这个环节里，人既是生产者，也是生产工具，还是生产对象。
en: In sex work, within this transaction, the person is at once producer, instrument of production, and object of production.

text: 这从根本上消灭了“人”和“劳动”两个基本概念的结构。
en: This fundamentally abolishes the very structure of the two basic concepts of 'human being' and 'labour'.

text: 人的主体性就此丧失了。
en: Human agency is thereby lost.

text: 为什么人类一定需要主体性？
en: Why must human beings necessarily require agency?

text: 这基于一种先验的前提，即人类，不是工具，不是手段，而是一切社会行为的最终目的。
en: This rests on an a priori premise: that human beings are not tools, not means, but the ultimate end of all social behaviour.

text: 人类所创造的社会财富，一定不应该是单纯的生理性交换，而应该要有知识，经验，情感等价值的流淌，否则，财富本身就无意义，而是奴化人类的数字工具。
en: The social wealth created by human beings must not be mere physiological exchange, but should involve the flow of values such as knowledge, experience and emotion; otherwise wealth itself is meaningless and becomes a numerical tool that enslaves humankind.

text: 人类具有不被单纯满足生理需求的欲望和欲求所左右，作为一种理性的存在的性质，这是我们区别于动物性的根本，只有在理性之中，自由意志才得以产生。
en: Human beings possess the nature of not being swayed by desires that merely satisfy physiological needs, as rational existences — this is what fundamentally distinguishes us from animality, and only within reason does free will come into being.

text: 我们同样听说过一句话，向下的自由不是自由。
en: We have likewise heard the saying: freedom that drags you down is not freedom.

text: 即使一个人每次“奖励自己”，上帝就给他降下一顿饭的生活费，我们也绝不建议一个人每天在家沉迷“奖励自己”，因为那是动物也能做到的事情。
en: Even if every time a person 'rewards themselves' God were to send down a meal's living expenses, we would still never recommend that someone stay home every day indulging in 'rewarding themselves', because that is something even animals can manage.

text: 如果有任何一个人因此而无法走进理性王国，那么我们就要打破这个奖励体系，顺便把上帝的脑壳也打出一个包来。
en: If any person thereby cannot enter the kingdom of reason, then we must smash this reward system, and knock a lump on God's skull into the bargain.

text: 否决性交易合法化，亦是如此。
en: Rejecting the legalisation of sex work is the same.

text: 很抱歉最终上升到了哲学，或许会让很多人不满意吧。
en: I am sorry it ultimately rose to philosophy; perhaps this will leave many people dissatisfied.

text: 但很多事情反复思辨和拷打之后，是必须要走到这里的。
en: But many matters, after repeated reflection and scrutiny, must inevitably arrive here.

text: 针对后来评论区里说，按摩/搓背/捏脚之类的手艺活，也都是人类用自己的器官（比如手）在换取价值，难道这也是对人的工具化吗？
en: As for a later comment-section remark: massage, back-scrubbing, foot-rubbing and the like — manual work where humans use their own organs (the hands, say) to exchange for value. Is this also turning people into tools?

text: 难道他们低人一等吗？
en: Are they any lower than others?

text: 讲不通啊。
en: That doesn't add up.

text: 好吧，我先说我的结论，是的，【按摩/搓背/捏脚】等不包含劳动工具为媒介，主要以身体交互出卖劳动换取经济的方式，从本论题的狭义语境说，的确也是【低人一等】的。
en: Very well, let me state my conclusion: yes. Practices such as [massage / back-scrubbing / foot-rubbing], which involve no intermediary labour tool and mainly exchange labour for money through bodily interaction, are, within the narrow context of this discussion, indeed also 'lower than others'.

text: 我举一个很简单的例子你们就会明白，在东南亚国家，很多仆人是要给主人上完厕所擦屁股、清洗屁股的。
en: I shall give a very simple example and you will understand: in Southeast Asian countries, many servants must wipe and wash their masters' buttocks after they use the toilet.

text: 我说擦屁股，你们可能觉得，是呀，的确低贱了，东南亚猴子不讲究。
en: When I mention wiping backsides, you may think: yes, that really is demeaning; those Southeast Asian monkeys have no standards.

text: 但是说搓背捏脚，大家就觉得，好像没什么啊，习以为常。
en: But mention back-scrubbing and foot-rubbing, and everyone feels it's nothing, just commonplace.

text: 为什么这两者会产生区别呢？
en: Why does a difference arise between the two?

text: 第一，是因为文化环境不一样，导致了见得少，产生了“奇观化”效应。
en: First, because the cultural environment differs, which leads to seeing little of it and produces a 'spectacularisation' effect.

text: 人家泰国啊柬埔寨啊或许觉得，仆人给主人擦个屁股就是很正常的啊，主人付钱了啊，养活仆人了啊，你们中国不也有小妹给老板捏脚吗，大家都一样啊？
en: The Thais or Cambodians might well feel it is perfectly normal for a servant to wipe the master's backside — the master pays, he keeps the servant fed. Don't you Chinese also have girls rubbing the boss's feet? Everyone's the same, no?

text: 第二，体力劳动涉及到人对人的取悦，只要不是亲密关系的表达，能够商品交易化的，都或多或少涉及到对人类主体性的剥夺，无非是程度的多少而已——捏脚小妹的遭受的目光和待遇或许比性服务者高，
en: Second, physical labour involves one person pleasing another. So long as it is not an expression of intimacy, anything that can be turned into a commodity transaction involves, to a greater or lesser extent, the deprivation of human agency — it is only a matter of degree. The looks and treatment endured by foot-rubbing girls may rank higher than those of sex workers,

text: 但高不到哪里去，别假装自己很清高一视同仁很尊敬她们，你尊敬她们是因为你去的少，你还不够油，不够暴发户，不够炫压抑，你经受过良好的教育，
en: but not by much. Don't pretend you are above it all, treating them impartially and respecting them. You respect them because you go seldom, because you are not slick enough, not nouveau-riche enough, not ostentatiously repressed enough — because you have had a good education,

text: 知道这是收入问题，短期内解决不了，除非你真的说我就是月入百万，我就支持女儿去给别人捏脚，那我真的相信你，人与人之间的器官劳动就是崇高的；
en: and understand this is an income problem that cannot be solved in the short term, unless you can truly say 'I earn a million a month and I would support my daughter rubbing other people's feet' — only then would I truly believe you, that bodily labour between people is noble;

text: 第三，从人类这一族谱的生物学源头看，猿类猴类都有帮同类族群清洁身体，尤其是抓跳蚤的习惯，但那仅限于同族群，而且是友好关系的亲密表达。
en: Third, from the biological origin of the human lineage, apes and monkeys all have the habit of helping clean one another's bodies, especially of picking off fleas — but that is limited to their own group and is an intimate expression of friendly relations.

text: 抛开亲密表达呢？
en: What if we set intimacy aside?

text: 只有猴王这种高人一等的才能享受任意猴子的抓跳蚤服务，因为他们的社会关系类似人类社会关系中阶级差距的变体，猴王高人一等，这就是一种高位者享受低位者身体服务的变体。
en: Only a monkey king, as one who ranks above the rest, can enjoy flea-picking service from any monkey, because their social relations resemble a variant of the class gap in human society. The monkey king stands above the others — this is a variant of the high enjoying the bodily service of the low.

text: 综上所诉，从本题的狭义语境出发，按摩/搓背/捏脚或多或少涉及到了对人类主体性的异化和侵犯，只不过由于社会文化传统的熏染+异化程度不深+政治叙事中的阶级矛盾已经消灭——导致我们认为，这种身体交互为基础的体力劳动是合理合法的，进而类比到卖淫合法。
en: To sum up, starting from the narrow context of this question, massage / back-scrubbing / foot-rubbing more or less involve the alienation and violation of human agency. It is only because of the influence of socio-cultural tradition, plus a shallow degree of alienation, plus the abolition of class contradiction within the political narrative — that we regard this bodily-interaction-based physical labour as reasonable and lawful, and from there draw an analogy to the legalisation of prostitution.

text: 这种类比，并不是非常完善的。
en: This analogy is not entirely sound.

text: 万一就是有人比较轴，说，老娘就是月入百万就是喜欢卖就享受这种心理和生理的快感不行吗？
en: What if someone is just stubborn and says: 'I earn a million a month and simply enjoy selling myself and the psychological and physical pleasure of it — what's wrong with that?'

text: 行，其实啊，很多地方的法律法规也考虑到了这一点，比如香港。
en: Very well — actually, the laws and regulations of many places have taken this into account, Hong Kong for example.

text: 香港就是卖淫违法，做楼凤不违法，所以每一个你能想到的角度，人类社会都有该理论下的试验田，但这些试验田究竟哪一种才是对的，哪一种是不对的，我相信历史会给出它的答案。
en: Hong Kong makes prostitution illegal, yet running a flat-based operation is not. So for every angle you can imagine, human society has its experimental plot under that theory — but which of these plots is right and which is wrong, I believe history will give its answer.

text: 我们讨厌国内的婚姻叙事和法制标准，是一个问题。
en: Our dislike of the domestic marriage narrative and legal standards is one issue.

text: 卖淫合法化，是另一个问题。
en: The legalisation of prostitution is another.

text: 不要因为被玫瑰刺伤而去伤害月季，就酱。
en: Do not, because you were pricked by a rose, go and harm a China rose — and that's that.
